content: Halls is a well-known brand of mentholated cough drops. These cough drops are classified by the manufacturer as both a cough suppressant and an oral anesthetic. They are produced and sold by the Cadbury-Adams Division of Cadbury-Schweppes. The origins of Halls date back to the 1930s in Britain, where they were first created by the Halls Brothers company, which was established in 1893. In 1964, the Halls Brothers company was acquired by Warner-Lambert, and later, in 1971, the Halls brand was purchased by Cadbury-Schweppes. Today, Halls is recognized as a global brand. Halls cough drops have been marketed for a long time as having vapor action, which is a feature that provides a cooling and soothing sensation. They are available in a variety of flavors, including Canada Dry Ginger Ale, Citrus Blend, Cherry, Honey-Lemon, Ice Blue Peppermint, Mentho-Lyptus, Spearmint, Strawberry, Tropical Fruit, and Pina Colada. Additionally, a Green Tea flavor is specifically available in China. The inactive ingredients in Halls cough drops include FD&C Red No. 40, flavors, glucose syrup, sucrose, and water. The Halls Defense line of products contains flavors that are fortified with Vitamin C to support immune health. Halls also offers a product line called Halls Fruit Breezers, which are non-mentholated lozenges designed to provide a pleasant taste. These come in flavors such as Cool Berry, Cool Creamy Orange, Cool Creamy Strawberry, Tropical Chill, and Cool Citrus Blend. For those seeking sugar-free options, Halls provides a sugar-free line of mentholated cough drops. Outside of North America, Halls is more commonly marketed as a mentholated hard candy rather than as a medicinal cough drop. In these regions, the product is manufactured in the form of hard candy and is not typically recognized as a remedy for coughs.
